chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from al-Halabi and Zurarah, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, that he was asked about prayer for the child: when is prayer to be performed upon him? He said:
When he understands salat (prayer). I said: And when does salat (prayer) become obligatory upon him? He said: When he is a son of six years, and sawm (fasting) is when he is capable of it.

key_terms.أَطَاقَهُ: is capable of it, meaning having the ability to bear fasting
key_terms.الصَّبِيِّ: the child, referring to the minor whose religious practice is being asked about
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: salat (prayer), the ritual prayer being discussed for the child
key_terms.الصِّيَامُ: sawm (fasting), the act of fasting discussed in relation to ability
key_terms.سِتِّ سِنِينَ: six years, the age mentioned for salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: When does salat (prayer) become obligatory for a child, and when is a child required to fast?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the age and capacity at which a child is addressed regarding salat (prayer) and sawm (fasting). It indicates that prayer relates to the child's understanding, with obligation stated at six years, while fasting depends on the child's ability.
